Distance-based kernels

Source: R/kernels_extended.R
k_dist.Rd

A kernel sigma^2 * phi(D / ell) on a distance matrix: patristic distances on the tree (the default) or any other distance between species, such as great-circle distances between range centroids for a phylogeny + space model (k_bm() + k_dist(geo) + k_white()). The component is dense, so models containing it use dense linear algebra (O(N^3)).

Usage

k_dist(
  D = NULL,
  phi = c("exponential", "matern32", "matern52", "sqexp"),
  lower = 0.001,
  upper = 10
)

Arguments

D

NULL for patristic distances on the tree, or a symmetric distance matrix with row and column names matching the tip labels.

phi

"exponential", "matern32", "matern52" or "sqexp".

lower, upper

Bounds for the length-scale ell, as multiples of the largest distance.

Value

A kernel component.

Details

Validity depends on the distance and on phi. On an ultrametric tree every non-increasing phi gives a valid kernel on patristic distances. On trees with fossil tips or without a clock only completely monotone functions such as the exponential are guaranteed valid; squared-exponential and Matern kernels can fail. Use kernel_check() before fitting.

Examples

k_dist(phi = "exponential")
#> phylogp kernel: dist(exponential) 
#>   dist1      dist(exponential)            parameters: sigma, ell
